items.title: Agentic cheminformatics with Google Antigravity
items.rationale: Primary-source release: DeepMind's Cheminformatics Skills let an agent go from literature mining to matched-pair analysis and macrocycle proposals with synthesis routes in about an hour. A new tool that changes how lab work is done.
items.excerpt: DeepMind's Cheminformatics Skills for Google Antigravity let an agent retrieve thousands of literature compounds, curate 568 into an interactive viewer, run matched-molecular-pair analysis and propose rigidified macrocycles with synthesis routes in about an hour. The post stresses designs still need experimental validation.

items.title: Tell this AI what you want a protein to do—and it designs one
items.rationale: Nature paper: Westlake's Pinal turns plain-language function descriptions into protein sequences, with wet-lab hit rates reported (best H-protein 1.7x natural). A different model and lab from the 10-24 Nvidia/UW story.
items.excerpt: Westlake University's Pinal model (Nature) turns plain-language descriptions into protein sequences via structural blueprints; 1 of 29 fluorescent candidates glowed and 5 of 20 H-protein candidates worked, the best boosting carbon-fixation output 1.7x over the natural E. coli protein.

items.title: Leading AI models are biased against certain accents when scoring interviews, presentations and tests
items.rationale: EMNLP 2026 study with a clean controlled design: the same AI-voiced answers in five accents, and four audio LMs rank Chinese and Nigerian accents lowest. A new, concrete bias finding about audio models.
items.excerpt: University of Washington researchers (EMNLP 2026) tested four audio language models on identical AI-voiced answers in American, British, Chinese, Indian and Nigerian accents; models ranked Chinese and Nigerian accents lowest even when content and transcription were identical.

items.title: StateBench: Testing how language models track state changes over long documents
items.rationale: New primary-source benchmark: frontier models drop to 13% or lower on long state-tracking, while small trained Gated DeltaNet/hybrid models generalize. A new release with a sharp, quotable result.
items.excerpt: Ai2's StateBench tests entity-state tracking over long inputs at four difficulty levels; frontier models fall to 13% accuracy or lower on the longest general problems, while small Gated DeltaNet and hybrid models trained on the task generalize to tens of thousands of assignments.

items.title: Machine learning helps track semiconductor defects under more realistic temperature conditions
items.rationale: Adds a materials-science pick: Chalmers (npj Computational Materials) uses ML to make temperature-dependent defect-level calculations feasible and finds shifts that absolute-zero models miss.
items.excerpt: Chalmers researchers (npj Computational Materials) used machine learning to make temperature-dependent defect-level calculations feasible, finding significant shifts that absolute-zero models miss.

dedup.note: Pool of 19, no cluster ids. Checked every candidate against the 30-day history_digest and all sections of published_urls.json (exact URL match): no candidate URL has been published in any section. history_match review: the Pinal protein story (related to the 10-24 Nvidia/UW protein model) is a different model, lab and paper, so it is new. GAP (npj, related to the 10-22 NZ downpours) is also a different story, but I left it out because nature.com is deliberately excluded from the science domain list. The Physics World astrobiology feature (related to 11-02 enzymes) is a different topic, but it is an evergreen feature, so I left it out. Excluded: FAU quantum ML lung-cancer prediction (clinical, belongs to medicine); FirstQFM (company claim about a financial-forecasting benchmark); Parse/Nomic dataset (vendor/business); Live Science 'could AI build itself' (evergreen, same theme as the 08-20 MIT TR recursive self-improvement story); SciAm voice-clone explainer (evergreen how-to); MIT TR mechanism-design piece (analysis); Pritzker prize (award; MIT News is not on the science domain list). Not picked for diversity: sycophancy, AI companions, empathy paradox (a third and fourth LLM-behaviour item would have stacked up next to accent bias and StateBench), olmOCR archives, deepfake light detection (10-21, older). Outlets: DeepMind 1, Phys.org 2, Tech Xplore 1, Ai2 1.
